stem: A methylphenidate Schedule II prescription is issued for an LTCF resident and the pharmacy will partially fill it over time under the federal special pathway. What maximum time framework applies from the prescription's issue date, unless it is discontinued sooner?

choices.text: A 60-day period measured from the prescription issue date

explanation.core_reasoning: A methylphenidate prescription for an LTCF resident can use the special C-II partial-fill framework for up to 60 days from issue.

choice_analysis.A: The 72-hour remainder rule addresses a different Schedule II partial-fill situation.
choice_analysis.B: Seven days is associated with an emergency oral Schedule II follow-up rule, not this LTCF endpoint.
choice_analysis.C: Ninety days is not the special federal LTCF/terminal partial-fill duration for one prescription.
choice_analysis.D: The LTCF/terminally ill Schedule II pathway permits partial filling for up to 60 days from issue unless discontinued sooner.
choice_analysis.E: Six months resembles other controlled-substance refill frameworks and does not govern this Schedule II pathway.

related_facts: The rule is not limited to narcotic Schedule II drugs.
explanation.mpje_trap: Choosing 72 hours because it is the most familiar C-II partial-fill clock.
